use super::file_name::QuoteStyle;
use nu_ansi_term::{AnsiString as ANSIString, Style};
use percent_encoding::{utf8_percent_encode, AsciiSet, CONTROLS};

pub fn escape(
    string: String,
    bits: &mut Vec<ANSIString<'_>>,
    good: Style,
    bad: Style,
    quote_style: QuoteStyle,
) {
    let bits_starting_length = bits.len();
    let needs_quotes = string.contains(' ') || string.contains('\'');
    let quote_bit = good.paint(if string.contains('\'') { "\"" } else { "\'" });

    if string
        .chars()
        .all(|c| c >= 0x20 as char && c != 0x7f as char)
    {
        bits.push(good.paint(string));
    } else {
        for c in string.chars() {
            // The `escape_default` method on `char` is *almost* what we want here, but
            // it still escapes non-ASCII UTF-8 characters, which are still printable.

            // TODO: This allocates way too much,
            // hence the `all` check above.
            if c >= 0x20 as char && c != 0x7f as char {
                bits.push(good.paint(c.to_string()));
            } else {
                bits.push(bad.paint(c.escape_default().to_string()));
            }
        }
    }

    if quote_style != QuoteStyle::NoQuotes && needs_quotes {
        bits.insert(bits_starting_length, quote_bit.clone());
        bits.push(quote_bit);
    }
}

const HYPERLINK_ESCAPE_CHARS: &AsciiSet = &CONTROLS.add(b' ');
const HYPERLINK_OPENING_START: &str = "\x1B]8;;";
const HYPERLINK_OPENING_END: &str = "\x1B\x5C";
// Combination of both above tags
pub const HYPERLINK_CLOSING: &str = "\x1B]8;;\x1B\x5C";

pub fn get_hyperlink_start_tag(abs_path: &str) -> String {
    let abs_path = utf8_percent_encode(abs_path, HYPERLINK_ESCAPE_CHARS).to_string();

    // On Windows, `std::fs::canonicalize` adds the Win32 File prefix, which we need to remove
    #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
    let abs_path = abs_path.strip_prefix("\\\\?\\").unwrap_or(&abs_path);

    format!("{HYPERLINK_OPENING_START}file://{abs_path}{HYPERLINK_OPENING_END}")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod test {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hyperlink_start_tag_escape_spaces() {
        assert_eq!(
            get_hyperlink_start_tag("/folder name/file name").to_string(),
            format!(
                "{HYPERLINK_OPENING_START}file:///folder%20name/file%20name{HYPERLINK_OPENING_END}"
            ),
        );
    }
}

 207:     def count(self, name: str) -> int:

 214:         wanted = set(names)

 216:             if occurrence.spec.long in wanted and occurrence.value is not None:

 237: def parse_argv(argv: list[str]) -> Parsed:
 238:     parsed = Parsed()
 239:     parsing = True
 240:     i = 0
 241:     while i < len(argv):
 242:         token = argv[i]
 243:         i += 1
 244:         if not parsing:
 245:             parsed.paths.append(token)
 246:             continue
 247:         if token == "--":
 248:             parsing = False
 249:             continue
 250:         if token.startswith("--"):
 251:             body = token[2:]
 252:             before = body
 253:             after = None
 254:             if "=" in body:
 255:                 b, a = body.split("=", 1)
 256:                 if b and a:
 257:                     before, after = b, a
 258:             spec = BY_LONG.get(before)
 259:             if spec is None:
 260:                 raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument --{before}")
===== 261-520 =====
 261:             shown = f"--{spec.long}"
 262:             if after is not None:
 263:                 if spec.takes == "forbidden":
 264:                     raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
 265:                 parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, after))
 266:             elif spec.takes == "forbidden":
 267:                 parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, None))
 268:             elif spec.takes == "necessary":
 269:                 if i >= len(argv):
 270:                     raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
 271:                 parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, argv[i]))
 272:                 i += 1
 273:             else:
 274:                 if i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
 275:                     value = argv[i]
 276:                     i += 1
 277:                 else:
 278:                     value = spec.default
 279:                 parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
 280:             continue
 281:         if token.startswith("-") and token != "-":
 282:             body = token[1:]
 283:             if "=" in body:
 284:                 before, after = body.split("=", 1)
 285:                 if before and after:
 286:                     for char in before[:-1]:
 287:                         spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
 288:                         if spec is None:
 289:                             raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
 290:                         shown = f"-{char}"
 291:                         if spec.takes == "necessary":
 292:                             raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
 293:                         value = spec.default if spec.takes == "optional" else None
 294:                         parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
 295:                     char = before[-1]
 296:                     spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
 297:                     if spec is None:
 298:                         raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
 299:                     shown = f"-{char}"
 300:                     if spec.takes == "forbidden":
 301:                         raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
 302:                     parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, after))
 303:                     continue
 304:             j = 0
 305:             while j < len(body):
 306:                 char = body[j]
 307:                 spec = BY_SHORT.get(char)
 308:                 if spec is None:
 309:                     raise OptionError(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
 310:                 shown = f"-{char}"
 311:                 j += 1
 312:                 if spec.takes == "forbidden":
 313:                     parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, None))
 314:                 elif spec.takes == "necessary":
 315:                     if j < len(body):
 316:                         value = body[j:]
 317:                         j = len(body)
 318:                     elif i < len(argv):
 319:                         value = argv[i]
 320:                         i += 1
 321:                     else:
 322:                         raise _flag_needs_value(shown, spec.choices)
 323:                     parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
 324:                     break
 325:                 else:
 326:                     if j < len(body):
 327:                         value = body[j:]
 328:                         if spec.choices and value not in spec.choices:
 329:                             raise OptionError(f"Flag {shown} cannot take a value")
 330:                         j = len(body)
 331:                     elif i < len(argv) and spec.choices and argv[i] in spec.choices:
 332:                         value = argv[i]
 333:                         i += 1
 334:                     else:
 335:                         value = spec.default
 336:                     parsed.occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec, shown, value))
 337:                     break
 338:             continue
 339:         parsed.paths.append(token)
 340:     return parsed

 344:     spec = BY_LONG[spec_name]
 345:     suffix = f" ({_choices_text(spec.choices)})" if spec.takes == "necessary" and spec.choices else ""
 346:     escaped = value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n")

 350: def _parse_usize(value: str, source: str) -> int:
 351:     if not value or not value.isascii() or not value.isdigit():
 352:         raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: invalid digit found in string')
 353:     result = int(value, 10)
 354:     if result > (1 << 64) - 1:
 355:         raise OptionError(f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {source}: number too large to fit in target type')
 356:     return result

 543: def _path_name(path: str) -> str:
 544:     raw = path.rstrip("\\/")
 545:     if raw and re.split(r"[\\/]", raw)[-1] == "..":
 546:         return ".."
 547:     normalized = ntpath.normpath(path)
 548:     name = ntpath.basename(normalized)
 549:     if name:
 550:         return name
 551:     if path in (".", ".."):
 552:         return path
 553:     drive, tail = ntpath.splitdrive(normalized)
 554:     return tail or drive or path

 573:     def lstat(self) -> os.stat_result:
 574:         if self._lstat is None:
 575:             self._lstat = os.lstat(self.path)
 576:         return self._lstat

 578:     def followed_stat(self) -> os.stat_result:
 579:         return os.stat(self.path)

 581:     def attrs(self) -> int:
 582:         st = self.lstat()
 583:         attrs = getattr(st, "st_file_attributes", 0)
 584:         if attrs:
 585:             return int(attrs)
 586:         result = 0
 587:         if _stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode):
 588:             result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY
 589:         elif _stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
 590:             result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE
 591:         if not os.access(self.path, os.W_OK):
 592:             result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY
 593:         if self.is_link():
 594:             result |= FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT
 595:         return result

 597:     def is_link(self) -> bool:
 598:         return _stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode) or bool(self.attrs() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT and os.path.islink(self.path))

 600:     def is_dir(self) -> bool:
 601:         return _stat.S_ISDIR(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()
 602: 
 603:     def is_file(self) -> bool:
 604:         return _stat.S_ISREG(self.lstat().st_mode) and not self.is_link()

 606:     def points_to_dir(self) -> bool:
 607:         if self.is_dir():
 608:             return True
 609:         if self.is_link():
 610:             try:
 611:                 return os.path.isdir(self.path)
 612:             except OSError:
 613:                 return False
 614:         return False

 623:     def time_ns(self, which: str, deref: bool = False) -> Optional[int]:
 624:         try:
 625:             st = self.followed_stat() if deref and self.is_link() else self.lstat()
 626:         except OSError:

 637:     return (a > b) - (a < b)

 640: def _natural_compare(a: str, b: str, insensitive: bool) -> int:
 641:     # natord ignores whitespace, compares ordinary characters directly, and
 642:     # compares adjacent ASCII digit runs by numeric magnitude.  Equal nonzero
 643:     # numbers with more leading zeroes sort first; an all-zero run retains the
 644:     # usual shorter-prefix ordering.
 645:     if insensitive:
 646:         a, b = a.lower(), b.lower()
 647:     a = "".join(char for char in a if not char.isspace())
 648:     b = "".join(char for char in b if not char.isspace())
 649:     ai = bi = 0
 650:     while ai < len(a) and bi < len(b):
 651:         ac, bc = a[ai], b[bi]
 652:         if "0" <= ac <= "9" and "0" <= bc <= "9":
 653:             ae, be = ai, bi
 654:             while ae < len(a) and "0" <= a[ae] <= "9": ae += 1
 655:             while be < len(b) and "0" <= b[be] <= "9": be += 1
 656:             arun, brun = a[ai:ae], b[bi:be]
 657:             asignificant, bsignificant = arun.lstrip("0"), brun.lstrip("0")
 658:             avalue = asignificant or "0"
 659:             bvalue = bsignificant or "0"
 660:             result = _compare_values(len(avalue), len(bvalue)) or _compare_values(avalue, bvalue)
 661:             if result:
 662:                 return result
 663:             if avalue != "0" and len(arun) != len(brun):
 664:                 return _compare_values(len(brun), len(arun))
 665:             if avalue == "0" and len(arun) != len(brun):
 666:                 return _compare_values(len(arun), len(brun))
 667:             ai, bi = ae, be
 668:             continue
 669:         result = _compare_values(ac, bc)
 670:         if result:
 671:             return result
 672:         ai += 1
 673:         bi += 1
 674:     return _compare_values(len(a) - ai, len(b) - bi)

 677: def compare_files(a: FileInfo, b: FileInfo, opts: Options) -> int:
 678:     field_name = opts.sort
 679:     if field_name == "none":
 680:         return 0
 681:     if field_name in ("name", "Name", ".name", ".Name"):
 682:         an = a.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and a.name.startswith(".") else a.name
 683:         bn = b.name[1:] if field_name.startswith(".") and b.name.startswith(".") else b.name
 684:         return _natural_compare(an, bn, field_name in ("name", ".name"))
 685:     if field_name in ("extension", "Extension"):

 801: def _display_parent(path: str) -> str:
 802:     # Path::parent keeps leading `.` and `..` components and the spelling of

1090:     widths = [display_width(c) for c in cells]

1093:     for cols in range(1, len(cells) + 1):

1097:             col = index % cols if across else index // rows
1098:             if col < cols:

1100:         used_cols = sum(1 for w in col_widths if w or cols == 1)
1101:         # For a one-row grid the crate makes the conservative assumption that
1102:         # every column is as wide as the widest cell.  Multi-row candidates
1103:         # use their actual per-column maxima.
1104:         if cols == len(cells) and len(cells) > 1:
1105:             total = max(widths) * cols + spacing * (cols - 1)
1106:         else:
1107:             total = sum(col_widths[:used_cols]) + spacing * max(0, used_cols - 1)

1111:             break
